findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — [P1, confidence 100] `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` paired with `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` models a byte-limit contract as five fixed geometric resizes, so any image whose encoded size remains above the configured byte cap after the fixed 0.8^5 scale sequence is rejected instead of being automatically downsized; the strongest rebuttal is that five resizes suffice for typical photos, but the byte size depends on format and entropy rather than dimensions, leaving PNGs and incompressible images outside the feature's guarantee.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — [P1, confidence 100] `if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` adds the automatic-downsize acceptance path with no test change that proves an oversize image is reduced below the configured limit before `Upload.create_for`, so regressions leave the feature's sole acceptance criterion unverified.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — [P1, confidence 75] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` sends `80%` to the animated `gifsicle --resize-fit` command, whose required `WIDTHxHEIGHT` argument rejects that geometry, so every oversized animated GIF fails resizing and is uploaded at its original size.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication.rationale: The finding accurately describes a real limitation in the new code at lines 63-68. The diff shows a fixed loop of 5 iterations that reduces image dimensions by 80% each time, but as the finding correctly notes, file size depends on format and entropy, not just dimensions. A PNG with high entropy or certain image types may not reduce below the byte threshold after 5 iterations of dimension reduction. This is a legitimate design concern about the feature's guarantee, though it's more of an incomplete edge-case handling than a bug - the code will still work, it just won't fulfill the 'automatic reduction' promise for all image types.
